prompt:
Background picture for a mid-1980s PC parser adventure game with 16-colour EGA graphics, redrawn cleanly at high resolution so that it can be traced into lines and flood fills afterwards. Palette: only these 16 fixed, fully saturated colours and nothing in between: black, dark blue, dark green, dark cyan, dark red, dark magenta, brown, light grey, dark grey, bright blue, bright green, bright cyan, bright red, bright magenta, yellow, white. Every shape is filled with exactly one flat, solid colour: no gradients, no shading, no highlights, no shadows, no texture, no noise, no dithering, no soft or blurred edges, no glow, no haze. Drawn like an early computer picture built from straight lines and flood fills: simple angular shapes with hard straight edges and stair-like diagonals, large plain areas, few objects, each object in two or three flat colours; details such as planks, roof tiles, paving joints, window bars and waves are bold solid lines in a darker or lighter colour, never hairlines. The dusk sky is a stack of flat horizontal colour bands with hard borders: black at the top with a few single white star dots, then dark blue, dark magenta, bright red, and a yellow band right at the horizon; the low clouds are flat elongated shapes in dark magenta and dark blue. The sea is one flat dark blue area with a few short horizontal strokes in bright blue, bright cyan and yellow. Naive flat side view like a stage set: perfectly horizontal horizon, no perspective depth, no vanishing lines, no foreshortening. Every shape must be big and simple: the picture will be reduced to 160 by 168 pixels, so no detail is smaller than one hundredth of the image width. Composition for a wide panorama crop: all important content lies between 12% and 88% of the image height; the strips above and below may be cut away. The harbour-master's cottage stands at the far left, the jetty with the two moored boats in the middle, the lighthouse on its rocky headland at the far right; the horizon lies at about 40% of the image height. The quay is a flat walkable floor of plain light grey stone paving with dark grey joints across the whole lower third, its front edge running parallel to the bottom of the image. The stack of crates and the coil of rope stand at the back of the quay beside the cottage. The iron lantern on its tall wooden post and the two barrels stand in the foreground at the very front of the quay on the right half, their bases at about 84% of the image height; between them and the water lies a wide free strip of plain paving. Light is shown only by colour: the cottage window and the lantern glass are plain yellow areas; the lighthouse lamp is only a small yellow spot without any beam or rays, and no smoke rises from the chimney (lamp light and smoke are animated separately). Not a painting, not a modern vector illustration, not modern detailed pixel art, not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a postcard.

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Line-art tracing sheet for a mid-1980s PC adventure game background. Redraw the attached reference picture as a clean black line drawing on plain white paper: keep its composition and every shape, position and size exactly as in the reference, but ignore its colours. The sheet will be traced line by line on a drawing tablet and then flood-filled with colour, so every area that has its own colour in the reference is enclosed by a closed outline without gaps: each band of the sky, each cloud, the sea, the headland, the lighthouse and its red band, the cottage wall, roof, door and window, each boat, the jetty, the paving, the crates, the barrels, the lantern post and the lantern glass. Only pure black lines of one constant, bold width on pure white: no colour, no grey, no filled black areas, no shading, no hatching, no texture, no stippling, no sketchy or doubled lines. Few, simple, angular shapes with straight lines wherever possible; small details such as planks, paving joints and waves as single straight strokes; stars as small black dots. The lighthouse lamp is only a small closed outline without any beam or rays, and there is no smoke above the chimney. Not a colouring book with decorative detail, not a comic, not an engraving.

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture.
